parts: Hi -- it's this issue:

check_BioGeoBEARS_run() says: STOP ERROR: 1 row(s) of the BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table are set to be 'free', but they have starting values ('init') outside of the specified min/max.

...this can happen e.g. if pieces of the example script are run out of order, or something similar.

Like the message says, type:

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table

...then see which "free" parameters have an initial starting value ("init") outside of the allowed "min" or "max".  Then change the init value or the min or max to fix it.

# E.g. to lower the min of "j" to 0.00000000001:

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["j","min"] = 0.00000000001

Cheers!
Nick

parts:
Hi - "works" just means a parameter is usable or not, not whether it is used. Ignore mx01r, it is a vestige of a long-lost idea.

The error you were hitting is that BioGeoBEARS does a check: for every free parameter, is its "init" in-between its "min" and "max".  

If you hit that error, you need to change init, min, or max, nothing else.  The "works" column is not relevant.

As with everything, when starting out it is safest to

1. Go back to the example script
2. Switch in your input files
3. Run the script without changing anything, and being careful not to skip lines.

Cheers!
Nick

Your BAYAREALIKE analysis estimated "d" at 5.0, which becomes the starting value of "d" for the BAYAREALIKE+J analysis, but the "max" for "d" in BAYAREALIKE+J is set to 4.9999999.  So, as the error message says, the starting value is outside the specified min/max.

Estimating "d" above 5 is pretty rare, that would mean expecting >5 events per millions of years, typically most trees have branch lengths of millions of years and an average less than 1 event per branch.  It may be that some of the super-short branches in your tree cause this.

Anyway, you would never want to report an estimate of 5 anyways, because that isn't the actual maximum likelihood estimate, it's just the upper boundary on your allowed parameter space.  

The solution is just to raise the max, I've done this for both models, see attached script -- have to run to class but I bet it will work now. Search "NJM" for my edits.

Cheers,
Nick

Your BAYAREALIKE analysis estimated "d" at 5.0, which becomes the starting value of "d" for the BAYAREALIKE+J analysis, but the "max" for "d" in BAYAREALIKE+J is set to 4.9999999.  So, as the error message says, the starting value is outside the specified min/max.

Estimating "d" above 5 is pretty rare, that would mean expecting >5 events per millions of years, typically most trees have branch lengths of millions of years and an average less than 1 event per branch.  It may be that some of the super-short branches in your tree cause this.

Anyway, you would never want to report an estimate of 5 anyways, because that isn't the actual maximum likelihood estimate, it's just the upper boundary on your allowed parameter space.  

The solution is just to raise the max, I've done this for both models, see attached script -- have to run to class but I bet it will work now. Search "NJM" for my edits.
